items.title: Along the 45th parallel: from rice fields and vineyards to pink oysters at the mouth of the Po
items.summary: Halfway between the North Pole and the Equator. A road trip along the 45th parallel, which crosses northern Italy from Montgenèvre to the mouth of the Po. Through a landscape once famous for its fog, where exotic birds now take flight
items.content:
Not even travelling down the Nile had I ever seen a sacred ibis, prince of the marshlands, with its black head and downward-curving beak like an unsheathed scimitar.

Yet here was a pair of them beside the main road, searching for frogs or insects in a ditch, beneath a warehouse on which someone had written: “We make fog here.”

Except there is hardly any fog left, really. It has been dried up by climate change and the near-disappearance of the pollution that once trapped droplets of water in that thick, suspended haze.

And so, travelling along the 45th parallel, kilometre after kilometre, a whole encyclopaedia of small discoveries gradually finds its way into my heart.

Along this imaginary line that cuts across northern Italy from Montgenèvre to the beach at Boccasette, where the Po flows into the Adriatic and pink oysters are cultivated in the lagoons between farmland and sea.

The 45th parallel, to be precise. Halfway between the North Pole and the Equator. Five thousand kilometres above your head and another five thousand beneath your feet.

As anyone travelling along the Milan–Genoa motorway or the A21 Turin–Brescia may happen to notice, just beyond the border between Lombardy and Piedmont, an orange-and-black sign marks this balance between the two extremes, between Cascina Chiozzo and a trotting-horse breeding farm.

Between Voghera and Casteggio, meanwhile, an overhead road sign announces the geographical divide and the entrance to the Oltrepò, a curious region where the climate sometimes resembles Saxony's and sometimes Yemen's, with temperature swings of up to 15 degrees Celsius that Pinot Noir grapes — ideal for traditional-method sparkling wines — positively adore.

Indeed, this is known as the wine parallel, or wine's “golden latitude”: an imaginary trellis stretching across the sky, along which grow the Cabernet vines of Bordeaux, the Viognier of the Rhône, the Nebbiolo of the Langhe and the Areni Noir of Mount Ararat.

And buzzing around it is Apis mellifera ligustica, also known as the Italian honeybee, which thrives here thanks to the abundance of alfalfa and the flowering encouraged by fluctuations in temperature.

In Casteggio, Luca Bonizzoni keeps 2,000 bee colonies producing the extremely rare indigo honey, with an almost weightless texture on the palate and none of the cloying sweetness.

In short, I had hoped this journey would have something exotic about it, but I had hardly expected quite so much.

At dawn, I drove slowly towards the rice fields of Livorno Ferraris: not marshes, but floating meadows the colour of mustard, while tractors with cage wheels stood in the shade of farmhouses, waiting to be put to work.

Without warning or an appointment, I knocked on the door of Tenuta Colombara, home to a museum dedicated to the mondine, the women who traditionally worked in the rice paddies, and where Acquerello, the rice aged for eight years so prized by chefs, is produced.

“When I started, people said it was impossible to cultivate rice beyond this latitude, because rice is a tropical cereal,” says founder Piero Rondolino, walking through the old stables lined with photographs taken in the area by Gianni Berengo Gardin.

Meanwhile, the sun breaks through the clouds, illuminating one of the chimneys of the Trino Vercellese nuclear power station.

In the 1960s, it was the most powerful in the world, outstripping its American and French counterparts and producing 13 times the electricity needed by the entire province of Vercelli.

Then came Chernobyl. The referendum. The hole in the ozone layer. Aerosol sprays. CO2. Renewable energy. And the most recent summer, the hottest of the century.

“Our rice fields don't seem to be in danger, though,” Rondolino explains. “For every tenth of a degree the temperature rises, I can increase production. And if the fields dry out earlier, I can sow the rice directly into dry soil.”

But that rule applies only here, in a region supplied with water by Europe's largest catchment basin.

Water flows constantly down from the Aosta Valley , reaches Ivrea and floods the fields through irrigation channels and a canal commissioned in the 15th century by Yolande of Savoy, the French wife of Duke Amedeo, an unfortunate man lost in mysticism and epilepsy.

If Livorno Ferraris takes its name from Galileo Ferraris, who discovered the rotating magnetic field and invented the alternating-current electric motor, Alluvioni Piovera owes its name to the flooding of the River Tanaro, which for centuries swept the settlement away whenever the waters rose.

“Even today, when we want to describe a marshy patch of land, we call it a tanaromorto,” says mayor Gian Piero Borsi, who governs this watery territory without any opposition on the municipal council.

At Bar 381, the only one left, another figure has come to greet me: a rather disdainful-looking gentleman with a shock of white hair and the boots of a country squire.

“Allow me to introduce Count Niccolò Calvi,” says the mayor. “We've been working together to make the village beautiful since 1975, and we still address each other formally.”

The count lives with his wife and their son Alessandro in Piovera Castle, a magnificent Visconti fortress surrounded by centuries-old gardens.

“It was the first historic residence to open to the public,” he explains, a pioneer of what has since become common practice.

There is a former lemon house for weddings, which he affectionately calls the orangerie, an enormous museum of traditional crafts and 60 rooms that hosts a huge escape-room game.

There is a gallery of natural sculpture displaying tree trunks in fantastical human and animal shapes.

And there is a curious workshop containing 3,000 drawings for 3,000 words, a paper-based game invented by the count and loved by schoolchildren, who visit in large numbers with their classes.

Beneath the coat of arms of the ancient family, it is time to say goodbye.

The count recommends stopping at Da Manuela, a restaurant with a legendary trolley offering 140 cheeses.

Then there is Bassignana, through which the VenTo cycle route linking Venice and Turin passes. Or Novi Ligure, with its Museo dei Campionissimi, dedicated to cycling champions Fausto Coppi and Costante Girardengo.

And since no one is following me along the broad road, I zigzag along the 45th parallel towards Cantine Ballabio, hoping to watch the sunset from the giant butterfly-shaped bench overlooking the family's vineyard.

And suddenly, in the trigonometry of things, this parallel universe becomes perpendicular and steep.

items.title: IceWM
items.summary: Article URL: https://ice-wm.org/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50478515 Points: 297 # Comments: 146
items.content:
IceWM is a window manager for the X Window System. The goal of IceWM is speed, simplicity, and not getting in the user’s way. It comes with a taskbar with pager, global and per-window keybindings and a dynamic menu system. Application windows can be managed by keyboard and mouse. Windows can be iconified to the taskbar, to the tray, to the desktop or be made hidden. They are controllable by a quick switch window (Alt+Tab) and in a window list. A handful of configurable focus models are menu-selectable. Setups with multiple monitors are supported by RandR and Xinerama. IceWM is very configurable, themeable and well documented. It includes an optional external background wallpaper manager with transparency support, a simple session manager and a system tray. IceWM is available on popular Linux distributions like Debian, Ubuntu, Arch, OpenSUSE, Gentoo, Slackware, CentOS, antiX, NixOS and on most *BSDs.

IceWM was created by Marko Maček in 1997 using C++. It is now maintained at Github .

IceWM is themeable . The visual appearance of icewm can be changed by a theme, which is a collection of settings and small images. Over 450 themes can be downloaded from box-look.org . Extra is a collection of 91 highlights. See icewm -i list .

IceWM is translated into three dozen languages. To improve the translation for your language at Weblate, first register an account either here or there , then update .

Report your icewm bugs on Github . Only report it once and give relevant details.

To install all package dependencies in one go use the following script.

IceWM is released under the terms of the GNU Library General Public License.

Contribute to ongoing development and support of IceWM by donating .

items.title: Cos’è un buon orgasmo?
items.summary: Sfatiamo subito un luogo comune: non esiste alcuna prova che limitare il numero di rapporti sessuali migliori la qualità degli orgasmi Leggi
items.content:
“Il sesso è come la pizza: anche quando è cattiva è sempre buona!”. La frase, resa famosa dal film Amici per gioco, amici per sesso (1994) di Andrew Fleming, riscosse un grande successo agli albori di internet. Sarebbe finita nei meme, nei poster, sulle magliette. Ma dietro questa battuta si nasconde un dibattito. Com’è stato notato, si tratta di un punto di vista strettamente maschile: per una donna il sesso “cattivo” è doloroso, umiliante, pericoloso, distruttivo. Anche quando c’è un orgasmo.

Mi permetto di tralasciare i casi specifici della disorgasmia (quando gli orgasmi sono dolorosi) o della sindrome da malattia post-orgasmica (quando gli orgasmi provocano malessere) per concentrarmi su esperienze più comuni. Prendiamo per esempio gli orgasmi forzati, studiati dalla psicologa Sara Chadwick dell’università del Michigan. Il suo lavoro si concentra sugli orgasmi coercitivi, ottenuti con la forza, sotto pressione o durante rapporti consensuali ma non desiderati. È una gamma di situazioni che dà le vertigini: alcuni partner si rifiutano di godere finché non gode anche l’altro, insistono, colpevolizzano, minacciano, si spazientiscono, ricorrono al ricatto emotivo, esigono un orgasmo per consolarsi, per tranquillizzarsi o addirittura per confermare un orientamento sessuale.

Al di là di questi casi gravi, Chadwick spiega che sull’orgasmo ci sono molte aspettative. Lo si deve raggiungere per dimostrare di essere una donna desiderabile o un uomo prestante (e dunque si è quindi tenuti a raggiungerlo al momento giusto, né troppo presto né troppo tardi). Da qui la mia domanda: è ancora una buona pizza quando l’impasto è plasmato dalle aspettative sociali e il condimento è fatto di piccole vergogne e grandi messinscene?

Gli orgasmi non hanno bisogno di alcuna pressione per fallire miseramente. Tutti vivono di tanto in tanto dei soufflé orgasmici, che si sgonfiano all’ultimo momento: orgasmi sprecati, deludenti, sfiancanti. Un’esperienza frustrante che può addirittura essere ricercata! Una dominatrice può decidere di rovinare un orgasmo, aspettando che il suo sub raggiunga le soglie dell’estasi, per poi rallentare o interrompere ogni stimolazione. Non solo la pizza non è cotta, ma bisogna pure mangiarla e ringraziare.

Vorrei tranquillizzarvi: gli orgasmi possono finire male, ma possono anche riuscire. In maniera più o meno eroica. I tentativi di costruire una gerarchia sono tanti: Freud mette per così dire su un piedistallo l’orgasmo vaginale, mentre le seguaci del sacro femminino preferiscono i cosiddetti orgasmi uterini. Il piacere prostatico sta vivendo un momento di gloria, ma alcuni si affidano esclusivamente alla stimolazione del pene. È quasi del tutto screditato l’orgasmo ottenuto tramite la masturbazione: clitorideo per le donne, meccanico per gli uomini. Ma tutto ciò è ancora frutto di pressioni sociali, motivo per cui vi propongo un metodo usato dagli scienziati.

Per valutare il vostro ultimo orgasmo, non c’è niente di meglio dell’ orgasm rating scale (la scala di valutazione degli orgasmi), inventata nel 2002 dai ricercatori Kenneth Mah e Yitzchak Binik. È un elenco di aggettivi a cui assegnare un punteggio da zero (fuori tema) a cinque (estremamente pertinente).

Partiamo dalla dimensione cognitiva e affettiva. Il vostro piacere è gradevole, soddisfacente, vi appaga? Siete estatici, esaltati, coinvolti, euforici? Descrivereste l’intimità emotiva con il partner come amorosa, tenera, intima, appassionata, simbiotica? Vi sentite rilassati, appagati, sereni?

Passiamo ora alla dimensione sensoriale. L’orgasmo si è costruito progressivamente, si è intensificato? Scorre, vi travolge? Vi provoca vampate di calore, tende a diffondersi? Direste che è fulmineo (come una freccia) o zampillante (come una fontana)? Palpitante, pulsante? Descrivereste gli spasmi come brividi, tremiti, fremiti?

A prescindere da tutto questo, la vostra mappa orgasmica varia di volta in volta, così come varia da persona a persona e anche a seconda del tipo di stimolazione. Uno studio spagnolo, condotto nel 2023 e pubblicato su Archives of Sexual Behavior , indica che durante un rapporto sessuale gli orgasmi sono percepiti come più intensi, più emozionanti, più intimi. Al contrario, la masturbazione prevale per un effetto calmante e rilassante. L’orgasmo migliore è quello più intenso, più lungo, più spettacolare o quello che ci regala l’emozione di cui abbiamo bisogno?

Va notato, fra l’altro, che le donne attribuiscono quasi sistematicamente voti più alti ai propri orgasmi rispetto agli uomini, il che si può spiegare in vari modi. O le donne provano più piacere, o abbassano l’asticella del godimento, oppure gli uomini sono più pudici nel descrivere le proprie sensazioni.

Il dato interessante di questa scala è che si distacca dalle misurazioni convenzionali, come quelle che mettono al centro la durata dell’orgasmo (che avvantaggia le donne) o la sua frequenza (sbilanciata sugli uomini). Questi metodi non solo non rendono conto della varietà delle esperienze, ma possono anche sfociare in una sorta di competizione, come nel caso dei gooners negli Stati Uniti.

Se non avete mai sentito parlare di questo gruppo, è del tutto normale. Il gooning esiste dall’inizio degli anni duemila, ma sui mezzi d’informazione è esploso nel 2025. Si tratta di avvicinarsi all’orgasmo rinviandolo il più a lungo possibile. Alcuni gooners parlano di trance che durano diverse decine di ore (avete letto bene). È la saturazione pornografica che permette di mantenere l’eccitazione: il gooner o guarda video su più schermi contemporaneamente, o divide lo schermo in un mosaico di video, oppure consuma montaggi ultraveloci di sequenze che scatenano l’eccitazione. Con un paradosso ulteriore: per i gooners l’orgasmo migliore è quello che non si verifica. A riprova che la ricetta del piacere resta un fatto personale (come dimostra il concetto di pizza hawaiana).

Se non esiste un buon orgasmo in assoluto, se non è quantificabile, possiamo comunque cercare di ottimizzare le nostre sensazioni in una sorta di pleasure-maxxing ? Sfatiamo subito un luogo comune: non esiste alcuna prova che limitare il numero di rapporti sessuali migliori la qualità degli orgasmi.

Non solo l’astinenza non ha alcun effetto seriamente dimostrato sugli uomini, ma nelle donne una pratica regolare tende addirittura a migliorare l’intensità orgasmica. In compenso si può “caricare” un orgasmo aumentando la propria eccitazione (cosa più facile a dirsi che a farsi), o praticare la meditazione per rafforzare la concentrazione (invece di pensare alla lista della spesa). Ci si può anche prendere cura della propria salute, dell’alimentazione, del sonno e delle relazioni.

Ma in fin dei conti non sono sicura che si debbano dosare, condire e riscaldare i propri orgasmi come se dipendessero da una ricetta culinaria. Un buon orgasmo è unico, mutevole, sconcertante, ed è meglio così. Le nostre vite pianificate nei minimi dettagli hanno decisamente bisogno di questo spazio di abbandono. ◆

items.title: Il futuro di Israele
items.summary: Secondo lo storico israeliano le elezioni hanno confermato che le politiche violente di Tel Aviv nei territori occupati e nella regione continueranno Leggi
items.content:
Ci sono due modi di interpretare i risultati delle elezioni israeliane . Uno è vederli come una sconfitta del governo del primo ministro Benjamin Netanyahu. Mentre prima aveva la maggioranza dei 120 seggi della knesset (il parlamento israeliano), lo schieramento di Netanyahu si è ridotto a una minoranza di 53 deputati. I deputati che si oppongono a Netanyahu, invece, hanno 67 seggi.

Se Israele fosse una democrazia, avremmo visto scene di festeggiamenti simili a quelle che ci sono state in Ungheria, Brasile e Serbia, dove le forze politiche con tendenze antidemocratiche sono state sconfitte. Ma Israele non è una democrazia e non si può dire con certezza che Netanyahu sia stato sconfitto.

Per formare un governo, uno schieramento ha bisogno del sostegno di almeno 61 parlamentari. L’unico modo in cui Netanyahu può ottenerlo è convincere partiti o deputati dello schieramento rivale a unirsi alla sua coalizione, cosa che è già riuscito a fare molte volte in passato. Collaborare con i partiti palestinesi, che hanno conquistato 19 seggi, è fuori discussione.

Per l’opposizione a Netanyahu il percorso più ovvio per formare un governo sarebbe una coalizione con i due partiti palestinesi. Ma questo significherebbe mettere in discussione l’apartheid israeliano. I principali leader dei partiti ebraici avversari di Netanyahu, compreso Gadi Eisenkot , hanno promesso che non lo faranno in nessun caso.

C’è un’altra opzione: cercare il sostegno dei partiti religiosi ortodossi, che finora si sono schierati con Netanyahu. Per garantirsi il loro sostegno, gli avversari di Netanyahu dovrebbero garantire l’esenzione dei giovani ortodossi dal servizio militare e assicurare finanziamenti per le loro istituzioni educative. Ma la principale promessa di Eisenkot in campagna elettorale era che avrebbe costretto i giovani ebrei haredi (ultraortodossi) ad arruolarsi nell’esercito. Non è molto probabile che cambi idea, ma in politica non si può mai dire mai.

C’è anche la possibilità di un “governo di unità” guidato da una sorta di alternanza tra le figure più importanti del campo pro e contro Netanyahu. Il problema è che, in base a una legge approvata qualche anno fa, finché è ancora imputato in un processo in corso Netanyahu non può fare il ministro; la sua coalizione però ha fatto in modo che, per assurdo, la norma non valga per il ruolo di primo ministro.

Dato che il processo per corruzione di Netanyahu è destinato a durare ancora a lungo, il meccanismo della rotazione (in base al quale in Israele i leader dei partiti di una coalizione si alternano alla guida del governo per un periodo stabilito) Netanyahu non potrebbe far parte di un governo in cui Eisenkot fosse il primo ministro. Questo significa che chiederebbe di essere il primo a guidare il governo, tenendosi aperta la possibilità di farlo cadere alla fine del suo turno.

L’ha già fatto in passato. Nel 2020 ha violato senza esitazioni un accordo di alternanza con Benny Gantz, che ingenuamente aveva creduto di poter diventare primo ministro dopo due anni. Ne sono risultate nuove elezioni, che Netanyahu ha vinto.

Infine, è molto probabile che nessuno dei due blocchi riesca a formare un governo, cosa che porterebbe a nuove elezioni entro sei mesi. Netanyahu e il suo governo rimarrebbero in carica fino al voto, anche se con poteri più limitati. Questo gli darebbe l’opportunità di riprendere le guerre contro l’Iran e la milizia libanese Hezbollah e di continuare le loro politiche violente nella Striscia di Gaza e in Cisgiordania , nel tentativo di conquistare più consensi e vincere le elezioni.

Questa è l’opzione preferita da Netanyahu, perché la sua sconfitta parziale alle elezioni del 27 ottobre è dipesa molto dalla mobilitazione senza precedenti degli elettori palestinesi in Israele e degli israeliani più liberal residenti all’estero, tornati in massa per votare.

Questi possibili scenari raccontano solo una parte della storia e non bastano a comprendere pienamente cosa significano i risultati elettorali per Israele, per i palestinesi e per tutta la regione. Ecco di seguito le conclusioni più importanti che se ne possono trarre.

La prima riguarda il futuro dei palestinesi cittadini di Israele. Se ci saranno presto nuove elezioni, potrebbero presentarsi di nuovo alle urne in gran numero. Ma se saranno ignorati ancora una volta e messi da parte dagli altri partiti politici, non ci proveranno mai più.

In questo caso sarebbe difficile per la leadership di questa comunità continuare a rimandare una decisione strategica, cioè scegliere a quale spazio politico appartengono i palestinesi cittadini di Israele: a quello israeliano o a quello palestinese?

Fino a oggi, gli arabi israeliani hanno dato una possibilità al sistema politico israeliano nonostante il suo razzismo, la sua tendenza all’apartheid e le politiche criminali nei confronti dei palestinesi. I partiti palestinesi hanno raccomandato Eisenkot per la carica di primo ministro al presidente Isaac Herzog, che gli ha affidato l’incarico di formare un governo.

Se posso azzardare una previsione – ma è solo una previsione – l’opposizione ebraica a Netanyahu non s’impegnerà davvero in un dialogo con i partiti palestinesi. Il suo messaggio a quel punto sarà che i palestinesi d’Israele non sono soggetti legittimi nella scena politica israeliana.

Se mi sbagliassi, questo sarebbe un momento incredibile e di grande cambiamento nella storia di Israele e della Palestina, ma sembra esserci pochissima speranza che le cose vadano in questo modo.

Ci sono anche altre lezioni che possiamo trarre da questa situazione, con la consapevolezza che si tratta di un momento di grande instabilità nella storia di Israele.

La prima e più importante è che chiunque formerà il prossimo governo di Israele proseguirà il genocidio a Gaza, la sempre più intensa pulizia etnica in Cisgiordania e le politiche aggressive nella regione. La continuità di queste politiche potrà essere interrotta o arginata solo se la regione e la comunità internazionale invieranno con chiarezza a Israele il messaggio che portandole avanti ci saranno conseguenze.

La seconda lezione è che la società ebraica israeliana oggi è attraversata da divisioni più profonde che mai, al punto che è impossibile mantenere un sistema politico stabile , un’economia fiorente e una strategia positiva nella regione e nel mondo.

La terza lezione è che l’isolamento internazionale di Israele aumenterà come risultato di questa traiettoria. E continuerà la presa di distanza dal sionismo tra i giovani ebrei di tutto il mondo, compresi gli Stati Uniti.

Infine, cosa fondamentale, tutto questo avrà conseguenze nel dibattito globale sul sionismo. La scelta del partito dei Verdi nel Regno Unito di designare il sionismo come una forma di razzismo (per quanto attualmente si tratti di un’eccezione ampiamente condannata) acquisterà legittimità nel tempo.

Queste elezioni e gli sviluppi futuri stanno rendendo evidente che oggi in Israele il sionismo implica l’esclusione dei cittadini palestinesi dalla vita politica del paese, prima ignorandoli e in futuro possibilmente negandogli diritto di voto.

Le prospettive a breve termine sono preoccupanti. Il messaggio generale che emerge dalle elezioni israeliane è che le politiche future del paese continueranno a minacciare la vita dei palestinesi nei territori occupati, dei palestinesi cittadini di Israele e delle popolazioni del sud del Libano e della Siria. L’instabilità nella regione aumenterà.

Per quanto terribile sia questo scenario, tuttavia, a lungo termine le crepe connaturate al progetto sionista si approfondiranno, cosa che potrebbe portare alla sua fine. Possiamo solo sperare che questo sarà l’inizio di una nuova realtà politica capace di garantire il benessere di tutte le persone che vivono nella Palestina storica e nella regione. ◆

items.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.summary: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs.
items.content:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December.

Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines.

Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee.

"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X.

Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily on 3 December, but also warned the panel could issue a subpoena to compel his testimony.

Three House of Representatives committees - on intelligence and foreign affairs and a panel on China - have also sent a letter to Huang summoning him for a closed-door interview on 1 December.

How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House

How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions

Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China.

A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee.

Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang.

On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive.

Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing.

Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday.

According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company.

Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close.

Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently?

The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal

Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort".

One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company.

It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said.

Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public.

Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared.

Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information.

The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures.

But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data.

Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO.

Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires.

Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia.

Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago.

Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector.

Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair

items.title: Brave Search API now accepts agentic payments via the x402 protocol
items.summary: Article URL: https://brave.com/blog/search-api-agentic-payments/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50477649 Points: 199 # Comments: 110
items.content:
The Brave Search API , our developer tool for building applications with data from the Web, is adding support for instant, pay-as-you-go, agentic payments enabled by the open x402 payment protocol. Developers and autonomous AI agents that specifically require agentic search can now programmatically query Brave's independent search index, ground agent responses, and settle requests in real time, which eliminates the need for traditional API key management.

Integrating x402 with the Brave Search API makes it easier for an agentic harness to leverage Brave Search API via a CLI wallet, as Brave runs its own facilitator accepting USDC on the Base blockchain, with acceptance on other networks and with other stablecoins incoming soon. This allows a Brave Search API user the ability to pay for LLM Context (agentic grounding) or general web search on-demand, without first creating an account and selecting a plan. Instead, simply transfer USDC stablecoin to your agent's wallet via the Base network and it's ready to access the same high-quality search results powered by Brave's search engine.

Brave Search API endpoints behind x402 require payment on every request rather than authentication. A request sent without payment receives an HTTP 402 Payment Required response that states the price of that search and the payment details needed to pay it. The agent signs a USDC payment for that amount and retries the request with the signed payment attached. Once the payment is verified, the search runs and results are returned with a receipt of the transaction that occurred on the Base blockchain.

Pricing follows Brave's published API rates: LLM Context, an API designed specifically for providing search context for agents, will cost $0.005 ($5 per 1,000). Additionally, web (search for humans), news, image, video, and local endpoints will also be available for $0.005 ($5 per 1,000). Gas fees for transacting on the Base blockchain will be covered for a limited time. Since each request carries its own payment, a Brave Search API account is no longer needed to use the service.

The easiest path to query via x402 is to install Purl Wallet, a Stripe-developed CLI wallet for your agent. Set up your wallet, top it off using Base-native USDC, and start querying today.

Ready to build pay-as-you-go search into your apps or AI agents? Check out our Brave Search x402 Proxy Documentation and explore: https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/documentation/guides/agent-payments

items.title: Australian footballers will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
items.summary: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
items.content:
Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said.

After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement.

Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August.

The men previously denied wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking.

Australian media reported that three women, understood to be adult entertainers, had alleged inappropriate touching during the incident at the Pullman Hotel and are looking into civil action.

"Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment," police said in a statement on Friday.

A fifth player, Riley Bice, who was also suspended by the club, had already been cleared by police.

A lawyer for one of the women said she was "devastated" by the police decision.

Jackson Pannam, of Slater and Gordon law firm, added that the move "does not amount to a finding that the incident our client reported did not occur, nor does it diminish the seriousness of what she says happened or its profound impact on her".

John Karantzis from Carbone Lawyers, acting for the other two women, told the ABC his clients were "very disappointed and distressed".

"My clients' civil claim is based on a different burden of proof, it is based on the balance of probabilities," he said.

Heeney welcomed the police announcement, saying the past three months had been "incredibly difficult for my family, [my fiancee] Steffie and those close to me".

"To my family and friends, your love and loyalty has meant more than words can do justice," he continued.

The Swans said in a statement that it had been "clear from the outset" that its decision to suspend the players was "separate from the police investigation, and it stands by that decision".

"The Club has commenced a comprehensive examination of its AFL program and is committed to acting on the findings and implementing meaningful change to build an environment that players, staff, members, supporters and corporate partners can be proud of," it said.

Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich told reporters it was "not a day for anyone to really celebrate" and "we're still looking very hard at the programme and understanding where we need to get better".

He said the club would be doing everything to "restore the standards that this club has held for a long period of time".

In a separate statement the AFL acknowledged the police decision and said it reserved the right to investigate should any further relevant information come to light.

items.title: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
items.summary: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.
items.content:
State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say.

More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau.

"The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman.

This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company.

US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim.

Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software.

According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet.

Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction.

A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims.

Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities.

The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user".

"It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday.

"If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

items.title: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
items.summary: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.
items.content:
Ukraine's president has welcomed a pledge from US envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, to include delegates from the European Union in the next round of peace talks with Russia.

European leaders have expressed deepening security concerns this week, and Volodymyr Zelensky said bringing them into the talks would ensure the EU has a "voice" in negotiations.

Kushner and Witkoff met Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday evening as part of a busy day of shuttle diplomacy - they met Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier, who said that Russia's position on the war - and its demand for territory - has not changed.

The meetings follow talks in Abu Dhabi last week that failed to reach a breakthrough in ending the war.

But Thursday did see Russia and Ukraine agree to another prisoner exchange - the largest swap yet since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.

Kushner said it would return "thousands of people to their families", but there were no further details over how many prisoners would be exchanged or when it would happen.

US envoys meet Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Putin in Moscow

Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine

Zelensky has for several years been calling for European delegates to be included in the peace talks, and says it makes sense because of Kyiv's longer-term ambition to join the European Union.

On Thursday, Kushner said that the US has been "working very, very closely over the past several months with Europeans and I think that that's been very important."

He added that he had stressed to Putin how important it was to have European delegates "at the table".

Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US government's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin.

Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent.

Earlier on Thursday, the EU's foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told the BBC's Newshour the presence of a European delegate showed the Kremlin "now realised that Europe is a big player".

Kallas also expressed doubts that there was Russian momentum towards a peace deal.

Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin told a host of European leaders gathered in Dublin on Thursday that he believed the security of the region had been "fundamentally reshaped" by Russia's war.

"Many member states [of the EU] feel an existential threat because of what has happened in Ukraine and the potential, if Ukraine was to fall, for further aggression on the European continent," he told reporters.

Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control.

Tensions between the US and Ukraine were on display on Thursday before Witkoff and Kushner's meeting with Zelensky.

Earlier, the Ukrainian leader said that the military was facing more "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones.

Starshield technology, which was developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX company for government and military use, has played a vital role in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line.

items.title: Why midterm vote-counting is taking so long in America's largest state
items.summary: Alaskans are still waiting for the full results, including in the close Senate race between Republican Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola.
items.content:
For the last few weeks, in addition to its usual payload of passengers, medicine, and supplies, Alaska Seaplanes has carried some unique cargo: ballots.

The regional airline is a piece of a complex logistical puzzle that sees Alaskans' midterms elections votes cast by mail and in person carried across the vast expanse of America's largest state, which is primarily connected by water and air rather than roads.

This considerable task explains why, a week after most US states knew their results in the midterms - in which the Democrats won back both chambers of Congress from the Republicans - Alaskans are still waiting for the Senate race to be called.

The victor in this close contest between the incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan and his Democratic challenger, former congresswoman Mary Peltola, could remain unknown until 18 November, when officials expect to have counted all eligible ballots.

"We do feel a sense of pride of making sure we do the job right - the really complicated job of getting all these ballots across thousands of miles in Alaska," Andy Kline, the marketing director of Alaska Seaplanes, which serves the south-eastern part of the state, told the BBC.

"We feel like we're part of the last leg of that journey of those ballots."

Some precincts in Alaska are able to communicate their initial results to centralised election offices on election night, allowing state officials and news outlets to report some preliminary vote tallies.

But it takes time for the full picture of how people have voted to emerge.

As well as having the logistical challenge of counting votes from across a state more than six times the size of the UK, there is a delay waiting for mail ballots to arrive, says Charles Stewart, an election expert at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

These are allowed to arrive up to 10 days later, or 15 days for overseas voters, if postmarked by election day.

Stewart said that election officials had "chosen to err on the side of getting it right rather than a rush to report the second and third tranches of ballots that get counted".

Regardless of whether ballots were cast in person or by mail, all of them eventually wind up in the state capital of Juneau – which is only reachable by plane or boat – for scanning and counting.

While more urban districts can get their materials on a plane late on election night, it takes longer for smaller or more remote parts of Alaska.

In some places, "you get someone who's basically running the election for their family and their neighbours because it's such a small village", says Scott Kendall, an election lawyer who previously worked on two campaigns for Alaska's other Republican senator, Lisa Murkowski.

In these smaller areas, ballots are sealed up in special envelopes or containers and sent it through the mail - which is where companies like Alaska Seaplanes comes in.

Ballots are put on the planes and sent to Juneau, where they then get dropped at the post office and delivered.

"It's part of our daily routine, just another couple of boxes," Kline said.

Once all the in-person and absentee mail ballots reach Juneau, election officials will complete their review.

If no candidate gets more than 50% of the vote in the first round, officials will quickly use ranked-choice voting to re-allocate votes from the lowest-scoring candidates to their voters' second choices.

Then Alaska will finally declare a winner for its Senate race, as well as contests for governor and US House of Representatives.

Adding to the suspense of who will win the Senate race is the question of whether another Republican candidate called Dan Sullivan, who was allegedly recruited by Democratic operatives , would affect the outcome. Results released so far suggest a low probability.

This week, President Donald Trump alleged Alaska's Senate election had been "rigged" due to the second Sullivan's involvement. His administration is appealing its rejected lawsuit to halt certification of the election over the issue, which a lower court dismissed.

Meanwhile, a judge has denied an attempt by Peltola's campaign to get information about how many absentee ballots election officials rejected, as well as information about those voters.

The state argued it had no obligation to share this data, and doing so would violate voter privacy.

While the result of the election is of the greatest importance to many, for people like Kline, the process is also key.

"We're all citizens," he said of himself and his colleagues.

"We all feel like we have skin in the game to make sure that our elections are accurate and timely."

Judge dismisses Trump administration's lawsuit over two Dan Sullivans in Alaska election

Alaska Senate candidate denies knowing about alleged plot to put two Dan Sullivans on ballot

items.title: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
items.summary: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.
items.content:
Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment.

"People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC.

After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter.

"Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion.

Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next."

Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022.

But within less than two weeks, federal forces marched triumphantly into Mekelle. The TPLF made what it called a "strategic withdrawal" from the city and Tigray's other main towns so the army encountered little resistance. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force.

Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements.

Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority.

Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat.

"The TPLF has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage."

Abraha Hailezgi, a scholar at Mekelle University, agrees. "The army lacks a clear political vision. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says.

Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost.

Instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC.

He says the TPLF "intentionally allowed the ENDF to advance deeper into the heartland of Tigray", where it can be isolated and confronted on favourable terrain. "We chose not to fight on terms favourable to the enemy."

The TPLF is preparing for a major counteroffensive, he says, adding that TPLF fighters have launched attacks against Ethiopian forces in several locations following their withdrawal from the region's towns, arguing that these operations demonstrated the group's continued military capability.

It is hard to get verified information from Tigray and the BBC is unable to report from there. But phone lines and the internet, which were cut when fighting broke out, have now been restored.

Residents in different parts of Tigray tell the BBC that fighting is continuing in central, northern and north-western parts of Tigray, with the use of heavy artillery and drone strikes.

Eyewitnesses around Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, report heavy fighting involving artillery and ground forces in recent days.

"We could hear heavy artillery fire from the Sheraro direction. People are concerned because there is no sense of security," a businessman tells the BBC on condition of anonymity. He adds that military convoys from both sides had moved towards Sheraro, while a motorcycle operator in the southern town of Yechila says military checkpoints are still active.

Memories of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war remain raw for many residents.

The conflict saw widespread human rights abuses and allegations of ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray, while estimates suggest the war claimed hundreds of thousands of lives.

As soldiers from Eritrea, accused of some of the worst atrocities in the previous conflict, and Ethiopia have reappeared in Tigray's towns, many residents describe a profound sense of fear and anxiety, saying the sight of the troops has reopened still-fresh wounds.

Military sources aligned with the federal army say operations against the TPLF are continuing, with recent fighting and troop movements reported in northern Tigray, near the Eritrean border, as well as across central Tigray's rugged highlands. They claim the TPLF's capabilities are being steadily degraded.

Security analysts and observers agree that unrest is likely to continue for some time. "I see a situation in which there could be a prolonged war in Tigray," Yared Tibebu, a well-known Ethiopian commentator based in the US, tells the BBC.

Yared argues that the TPLF has a long history of waging protracted armed struggles and believes the movement is once again preparing for a lengthy conflict. He believes that once the group has reorganised its military and political structures, it may attempt to resume offensive operations.

However he believes this will not happen for some time because of internal divisions - a suggestion dismissed by TPLF spokesperson Mikael.

Hudson rejects the idea that Tigray is heading towards a prolonged war but agrees that the region may not be truly peaceful for some time. "The TPLF may continue a low-level insurgency and guerrilla campaign, but that is not war. I do not think there will be a wider-scale conflict between the federal forces and the TPLF."

He says the TPLF no longer possesses the size, strength or military capability required to effectively confront federal forces, which he says have significantly expanded and modernised in recent years. "The TPLF has also lost much of its public support and cannot easily rebuild its ranks through recruitment," he says.

Yared, on the other hand, points to the TPLF's history of overcoming setbacks as evidence that the movement could recover to sustain a prolonged struggle. "The TPLF has overcome many major challenges in the past. It is wrong to conclude that it has no public support. It is a political movement with a history stretching back more than 50 years," he says.

What Yared sees as a strength, Hudson sees as a weakness, saying the TPLF is still "trapped in the past", and continues to behave as a dominant party within Tigray, even though the situation has changed. "It is a movement that has not evolved, modernised or expanded."

While Hudson argues that the TPLF is not equipped to sustain a major military campaign, the TPLF spokesman says the group obtains weapons and logistical supplies from the Ethiopian military. "We seize weapons from our enemy, and the weaponry that has entered Tigray will, sooner or later, become ours."

In early October, eyewitnesses told the BBC they had seen Eritrean troops in Tigray amid reports they were backing the TPLF . However, they appear to have returned home and Hudson thinks the country would be wary of becoming further embroiled in the conflict.

"First, Eritrea does not have unlimited resources. Second, the TPLF is no more an effective military force, and Eritrean leaders may have concluded that supporting it at this stage would not yield significant military gains," he says. "Third, Eritrea would have to consider the risk of provoking a confrontation with Ethiopia if it openly backs the TPLF."

Sources in the Ethiopia army tell the BBC that senior members of the TPLF's political leadership were briefly based in Eritrea, however, they say the authorities ordered them to leave in early November, shortly after President Isaias Afwerki returned from Russia. According to the sources, the move was driven by concerns that Ethiopia could use their presence as a reason to invade.

Hudson also argues that Eritrea's renewed diplomatic engagement with the US, whose relations with the TPLF have long been strained, could further discourage Asmara from providing meaningful support to the movement.

In September, seven Ethiopian rebel groups led by the TPLF announced the formation of a new coalition called the Alliance for Survival, aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government.

Yared believes the alliance could give the TPLF the strength to keep on fighting. "Its members can combine their strengths. The TDF [the TPLF's military wing] has leadership experience and organisational capacity, while Fano [an ethnic Amhara militia] is believed to have between 70,000 and 80,000 fighters.

"If conditions emerge that allow the forces to co-ordinate effectively, the TPLF's current difficulties may not last long," he says.

items.title: Military cemetery decorum: The tradition behind Hegseth's Veterans Day reprimand
items.summary: BBC's Bernd Debusmann breaks down why Defence Secretary Hegseth's group was reprimanded at Arlington National Cemetery and the history behind its strict rules of conduct.
items.content:
Earlier this week, a sentinel reprimanded a group that included US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at Arlington National Cemetery. The incident followed a wreath-laying ceremony marking Veterans Day.

The Pentagon have since announced that Hegseth has given the soldier, Specialist Thomas Iglesias, a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier".

BBC's Bernd Debusmann breaks down why Hegseth's group was reprimanded, the history behind the strict rules governing visitor behaviour and the importance of maintaining an atmosphere of silence at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia. Bild: “Mosca chiede Finlandia fuori dalla Nato”. Cremlino nega
items.summary: Presidenza Ue: “Decidere entro due settimane chi rappresenta l’Europa al tavolo dei negoziati”. Esplode auto a Mosca: “Ferito il consigliere dell'ex premier ucraino Azarov”. A Dublino Witkoff e Kushner. Drone russo danneggia struttura sanitaria a Kiev, 3 feriti e decine di evacuati
items.content:
In corso a Dublino il Consiglio europeo informale, sul tavolo IA e conflitto in Ucraina. Da scioglire il nodo del rappresentante dell’Ue per i colloqui, Kaja Kallas contro il modello Kushner-Witkoff: “Noi abbiamo delle istituzioni, quindi non possiamo mandare una persona che non ha alcun ruolo istituzionale, come fanno gli americani. Non dobbiamo copiare gli stessi schemi”. Auto esplode a Mosca, ferito il consigliere dell’ex premier ucraino Azarov.

Bild: “Mosca chiede Finlandia fuori dalla Nato e Moldavia divisa”

Kallas: “Discutere ora di sicurezza europea significa cadere nella trappola russa”

Esplode auto a Mosca: “Ferito il consigliere dell'ex premier ucraino Azarov”

Presidenza Ue: “Decidere entro due settimane chi rappresenta l'Europa sull’Ucraina”

Drone russo danneggia struttura sanitaria a Kiev, 3 feriti e decine di evacuati

Euroclear: “Trasferire gli asset russi non elimina i rischi”

Trasferire i 185 miliardi di euro di beni russi congelati presso Euroclear all'Ue o a un altro organismo per finanziare l'Ucraina non eliminerebbe i rischi per la società belga. Lo afferma la direttrice generale di Euroclear, Valérie Urbain, in un'intervista a Le Soir, spiegando che, anche se il denaro venisse trasferito insieme agli obblighi di rimborso, la Banca centrale russa potrebbe continuare a reclamarlo a Euroclear. "Non esiste ancora una soluzione miracolosa", avverte Urbain, sottolineando che sarebbero necessarie garanzie finanziarie degli Stati membri fino alla fine della guerra o alla cessazione dell'obbligo di restituzione. In caso di gravi difficoltà della società, anche i contribuenti belgi potrebbero essere chiamati a intervenire. Per Urbain, il modo migliore di utilizzare gli attivi russi resta inserirli nei negoziati di pace: "Sono probabilmente la principale moneta di scambio di cui dispone l'Europa".

Cremlino nega di aver chiesto il ritiro della Finlandia dalla Nato: “Non se n'è parlato”

Il Cremlino smentisce di aver chiesto l'uscita dalla Nato della Finlandia, né di altri Stati membri dell'Alleanza, durante i negoziati ad Abu Dhabi sull'Ucraina. "Non ne sono a conoscenza. No, non è stata avanzata alcuna proposta in tal senso. Di certo non se n'è parlato", ha affermato il portavoce presidenziale Dmitry Peskov, rispondendo a una domanda in merito, citato dalla Tass.

Bild: “Mosca chiede Finlandia fuori dalla Nato e Moldavia divisa”

La Finlandia fuori dalla Nato, la Moldavia riorganizzata in tre repubbliche separate, zero truppe europee in Ucraina, il mantenimento dei territori occupati e il controllo dell'intero Donbass. Secondo la 'Bild' sono queste le proposte avanzate dalla Russia ad Abu Dhabi per porre fine alla guerra in Ucraina, che includono numerose richieste che vanno ben oltre i confini dell'Ucraina.

Merz a Trump: “No a sorprese su incontro con Putin, resti con Europa”

Il cancelliere tedesco Friedrich Merz ha chiesto al presidente americano Donald Trump di restare al fianco degli alleati europei e dell'Ucraina in vista del suo previsto incontro con il presidente russo Vladimir Putin, la prossima settimana in Cina. A margine del vertice dei leader Ue a Dublino, riporta Ntv, Merz ha riferito che alcuni temono che il colloquio possa trasformarsi in "un secondo momento Anchorage", - con riferimento al criticato incontro in Alaska tra Trump e Putin - con un'intesa tra Washington e Mosca raggiunta senza il coinvolgimento degli europei e di Kiev. "Voglio ribadire con molta chiarezza il nostro messaggio agli Stati Uniti: per favore, niente sorprese. Continuate a giocare nella squadra europea e in quella dell'Ucraina e lavoriamo insieme per una pace autentica", ha dichiarato Merz. "Questo è il nostro obiettivo e intendiamo mantenerlo". Trump, Putin e il presidente cinese Xi Jinping dovrebbero incontrarsi la prossima settimana a margine del vertice dell'Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) in Cina.

Il governo tedesco ha annunciato che giovedì 19 novembre si terrà un vertice della Coalizione dei Volonterosi, che riunisce gli alleati dell'Ucraina, per discutere degli sforzi diplomatici in corso per porre fine alla guerra scatenata da Mosca. L'incontro, su invito del cancelliere Friedrich Merz, del Presidente francese Emmanuel Macron e del primo ministro britannico Andy Burnham, verterà sul continuo sostegno a Kiev, sugli "sforzi diplomatici in corso" e sulle "garanzie di sicurezza per l'Ucraina dopo la guerra". Il vertice seguirà la ripresa dei colloqui russo-ucraini, mediati dagli Stati Uniti ad Abu Dhabi questa settimana, i cui risultati finora sono stati modesti. Si terrà anche nel momento in cui gli Stati Uniti vogliono che gli europei siano al tavolo dei negoziati sull'Ucraina, cosa su cui Mosca è ancora molto riluttante. Inoltre, la Russia, che considera la NATO come una minaccia esistenziale e quindi vuole indebolire l'organizzazione, chiede di legare la fine della guerra in Ucraina alla negoziazione di una nuova architettura di sicurezza europea, cosa che gli europei rifiutano. "La Russia vuole parlare delle questioni relative a un'architettura di sicurezza europea. Non è necessario discuterne, esiste già", ha detto Merz a Dublino.

Zelensky: “Ancora limitazioni a Starshield ma da gli Usa non arrivano spiegazioni”

"Non ci sono ancora spiegazioni chiare. Ho incaricato il ministero degli Esteri e il ministro della Difesa di intensificare i contatti con il dipartimento di Stato, il Pentagono e SpaceX per ottenere chiarimenti e risolvere la situazione". Lo scrive su X il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky sostenendo che gli americani non hanno fornito spiegazioni chiare in merito alle ragioni della limitazione dell'attività di Starshield al fronte. Secondo Zelensky, il comandante in Capo delle Forze Armate ucraine ha riferito di aver avuto contatti con la controparte americana in merito alla questione, ma senza aver risolto nulla.

Merz: “Berlino sarà a negoziati, non serve discutere dell’architettura della sicurezza europea”

"E' scontato" che la Germania sia a negoziati sulla guerra in Ucraina. A dirlo è il cancelliere tedesco Friedrich Merz in conferenza stampa a Dublino. "La Russia vuole discutere delle questioni relative all'architettura di sicurezza europea. Non c'è bisogno di parlarne. Esiste già", ha affermato quindi Merz, sottolineando: "È stata Mosca, e solo Mosca, a distruggere l'ordine di pace di Helsinki".

Cremlino: “Convinti che il prossimo round di colloqui sull'Ucraina si terrà presto”

Mosca prevede che il prossimo round di colloqui trilaterali tra le delegazioni di Russia, Stati Uniti e Ucraina per la risoluzione del conflitto si terrà presto, ha dichiarato il portavoce presidenziale russo, Dmitry Peskov. "Prevediamo che si terrà abbastanza rapidamente, in un futuro prevedibile", ha affermato Peskov, citato da Tass. "Questo è esattamente ciò che abbiamo discusso con i nostri negoziatori americani e quindi speriamo che i colloqui possano effettivamente proseguire in un futuro prevedibile", ha aggiunto il portavoce del Cremlino

Il Cremlino: “L’Europa coinvolta nei negoziati quando chiarirà di volere la pace”

Il portavoce del Cremlino, Dmitry Peskov, ha dichiarato che gli europei potrebbero essere coinvolti nei negoziati sull'Ucraina "quando vedremo che hanno l'intenzione sincera di contribuire al processo di pace"

Cremlino: “Non cambieremo la composizione della nostra delegazione negoziale”

La Russia non intende cambiare la composizione della propria delegazione ai negoziati trilaterali sulla soluzione del conflitto in Ucraina. Lo ha dichiarato il portavoce presidenziale russo, Dmitry Peskov. "Non ci sono le condizioni per cambiare la composizione. La composizione è stabile, almeno da parte nostra", ha dichiarato il portavoce del Cremlino, citato da Tass.

Il Cremlino: “Putin non ha mai rifiutato contatti con l’Ue, gli europei hanno interrotto il dialogo”

"Putin non ha mai rifiutato i contatti con l'Unione Europea. Sono stati gli europei a interrompere il dialogo". Ad affermarlo, secondo quanto riferisce l'agenzia di stampa russa 'Tass', è il portavoce del Cremlino Dmitrij Peskov.

Kallas: “I russi non mi vogliono? Noi non decidiamo per loro”

Riguardo alla discussione sul negoziatore europeo per l'Ucraina, "so che i russi non mi vogliono, ma, insomma, abbiamo forse voce in capitolo su chi rappresenta la Russia? No, non ce l'abbiamo". Lo ha dichiarato l'Alta rappresentante dell'Ue per la Politica estera, Kaja Kallas, all'arrivo al Consiglio europeo informale a Dublino.

Kallas: “Sono io a rappresentare la politica estera dell’Ue”

"Tutti gli Stati membri hanno in effetti concordato che sono io a rappresentare l'Europa in materia di politica estera e di sicurezza". Lo ha dichiarato l'Alta rappresentante dell'Ue per la Politica estera, Kaja Kallas, all'arrivo al Consiglio europeo informale a Dublino. "Nel giugno del 2024 c'è stata una decisione dei leader su chi rappresenta l'Unione quando si tratta di sicurezza e politica estera. E si discuteva del fatto che in questi cinque anni ci sarebbe stato un negoziato con i russi. Quindi, se i leader vogliono cambiare quell'accordo, naturalmente possono farlo, perchè è una decisione che spetta a loro. Ma penso che dovremmo concentrare le nostre energie, piuttosto, sulla sostanza", ha aggiunto.

items.title: Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer
items.summary: Article URL: https://edge0.ai/blog/introducing-edge0-145b-frontier-ai-capabilities-on-your-own-computer Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50475713 Points: 305 # Comments: 91
items.content:
Today, we're open-sourcing Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B , together with our unified inference framework and deployment tools. Edge0-145B is the world's first open-source on-device AI model with 145 billion parameters. It brings coding, reasoning, and agent capabilities that rival frontier cloud models to your own computer.

On-device AI has long forced a tradeoff between model capability and what the hardware can run. Larger models demand more memory, bandwidth, and power; smaller models can struggle with complex work. Moving that work to the cloud adds model-provider fees, data-handling constraints, and a dependence on connectivity.

We're releasing the full stack so developers can reproduce the results, evaluate or fine-tune the models, and integrate them into their own products.

Get the model weights , explore the inference framework , or try the Edge0 App .

Edge0-145B makes a 145-billion-parameter model usable on a personal laptop. A useful local model has to fit in memory, process prompts promptly, generate fast enough to use, and keep power consumption under control. It also needs to sustain longer tasks.

Our earlier Edge0-35B phone release reported peak memory below 2.5GB. On an iPhone 18 Pro Max, Edge0-35B delivers 37+ tokens/s using approximately 2.5GB of memory. Edge0-145B has roughly four times as many parameters; its laptop comparison reports 80+ tokens/s and 28GB peak memory. These measurements apply to different models and hardware.

On-device model scale over time. The chart covers 67 open models of at least 1B parameters from 14 labs, intended for phones, laptops, and AI PCs. Same-size base, instruct, and reasoning variants count once; each line tracks a lab's largest model, including releases before July 2025. Filled points mark new highs and hollow points other releases. The scale is logarithmic below 40B and linear above it. Apple is excluded because its weights are not released. Sources: vendor announcements and model cards.

Memory limits kept most on-device models below 10B parameters before September 2026. Apple Intelligence's on-device foundation model had approximately 3B parameters, while Google's Gemini Nano came in 1.8B and 3.25B versions. Even a 7B model could consume approximately 4GB of memory.

Larger models faced a memory wall. Model weights occupy storage and must be read during generation, competing for limited memory and bandwidth with the operating system and other apps. Even an aggressively compressed 35B model could need approximately 20GB of memory, far more than a phone could make available.

Compute, bandwidth, and power created competing constraints. Larger models offered more capability, but strained memory capacity, generation speed, and battery life. Making models smaller helped them fit, often at the cost of capability.

Privacy alone could not close that gap. Apple Intelligence protected user data, but Apple acknowledged that its on-device model was not designed for agentic applications requiring general world knowledge. The prevailing assumption was that on-device intelligence could not match the cloud.

We designed Edge0-145B and its inference engine together to reduce the memory and data movement that make large models difficult to run locally. The design spans architecture, training, loading, and scheduling.

Architecture: share large matrices across sparse experts. Sharing matrices substantially reduces the weights that must be stored and moved while keeping the expert count unchanged. Each group of 64 experts shares two large matrices, while each expert retains a small set of parameters that captures its differences. Previously, every expert stored a complete set of matrices. Of the model's 145B total parameters, only approximately 10B participate in computation on each inference step.

Training: build for local execution from day one. We train the model in its on-device architecture from the outset, with deployment constraints built into its design. This avoids treating local deployment as a compression or pruning step after training a cloud model.

Loading: pipeline GPU memory, system memory, and SSD access. Reading and computation overlap across three storage tiers, avoiding serial waits. Frequently used “hot experts” remain in GPU memory. An expert library of approximately 40GB sits in system memory, with experts brought into GPU memory as needed. Approximately 48GB of vocabulary data resides on the SSD and is read on demand.

Scheduling: use the CPU and GPU together. The GPU computes cached experts while the CPU handles the remaining work in parallel. Speculative decoding verifies multiple candidate tokens at once, spreading the cost of reading weights across more output tokens. These choices support the reported 80+ tokens/s decode rate.

Model and inference-engine design work together to make 100B+ parameter inference practical on personal computers. Source: internal testing.

Together, these changes let parameter counts grow from tens of billions to more than a hundred billion without proportional increases in memory use, power consumption, and latency.

Edge0-145B can carry a complex task through to a usable result. Its coding and reasoning capabilities support local workflows that combine planning, tool use, execution, debugging, and visual checks. The benchmarks establish its capabilities; the demonstrations show how it puts them to work.

Edge0-145B is competitive with specific frontier cloud models across coding, reasoning, knowledge, and instruction following:

Its 86.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 also exceeds Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's 83.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731's 82.7, and Claude's 78.2. On AA-LCR, Edge0-145B scores 79.3 to Claude's 78.0. These comparisons apply to the named models and evaluations.

Scores are percentages; higher is better. A dash means no public score is available, rather than a score of zero.

Edge0, Qwen, DeepSeek, and Claude results come from Edge0's internal evaluations. Claude-Opus-4.6 has no public DeepSWE 1.1 score. For Flint, Muse Glimmer, and Gemma 4, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and IFBench results come from the Recursive Flint evaluation; HLE, GPQA, and AA-LCR results come from Artificial Analysis.

The largest gains over Qwen3.8-27B, a mainstream on-device model baseline, are in agent and coding work: 18.5% on Terminal-Bench and 53.1% on DeepSWE . The relative gains on HLE, GPQA, and IFBench are 14.9%, 1.3%, and 1.4%, respectively.

DeepSWE 1.1 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 evaluate agent and coding work. HLE, GPQA-Diamond, and IFBench cover reasoning, knowledge, and instruction following. The complete evaluation setup, hardware environment, and reproduction instructions are being released with our technical report.

Edge0-145B combines a 72.8 mean score across six benchmarks with 29GB measured peak memory . Qwen3.8-Flash-Next averages 71.7, with an estimated 70GB footprint for standard 4-bit deployment. That puts Edge0-145B at about 40% of the estimated baseline memory while delivering comparable or higher capability, enabling local use on a 48GB laptop.

The means cover DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1, HLE, GPQA-Diamond, IFBench, and AA-LCR. Edge0 memory figures are measured internal peaks. Asterisked baseline figures are estimates for standard 4-bit deployment and remain to be measured. Claude is excluded because it is cloud-only and has no DeepSWE score.

[Figure: Quality versus peak memory, with 48GB laptop and 64GB workstation capacities marked. Lower memory and higher scores are better; the chart's vertical axis does not start at zero.]

A single natural-language request can start an entire local workflow. Edge0-145B breaks down the requirements, plans the steps, writes code, and calls tools to run it. When something fails, it debugs and repairs the code. It then takes screenshots to inspect the result and keeps iterating until the work is complete.

These projects often take dozens of rounds of planning, execution, and review. Local inference means those additional conversations, code revisions, and visual analyses incur no corresponding cloud-model token or API charges. Code and data can stay on the computer, and core model capabilities work offline.

Edge0-145B produced an explainer about how Roadster could fly, handling technical research, scriptwriting, asset generation, and editing. We asked it to make the principles understandable to a general audience. The model ran locally without cloud-model calls or cloud token consumption, avoiding network round trips for inference.

The video was generated within an hour. Producing comparable work manually would have taken a director and scriptwriter, a 3D modeler, an editor, and a physics expert a month. An AI video workflow could previously cost more than hundreds of dollars; local inference eliminates the corresponding cloud-model token and API fees.

Edge0-145B built a 3D scene of Manhattan within an hour. Working in Blender from text and reference images, it constructed the scene, adjusted materials and lighting, and iterated on the rendered output.

The workflow brings visual inspection, code generation, and revision together inside Blender. The model works with objects, spatial relationships, and the creative goal, going beyond the pixels in a reference image. It inspects the result, writes code, and makes changes without handing those steps back to a person. The entire process stays local.
